title: Prince Andrew in 'secret deal with business giant' to make millions from his sharing his high-profile contacts
text:
By Ayaat Yassin-Kassab
Published: 02:12 GMT, February 9, 2025 | Updated: 02:12 GMT, February 9, 2025
Prince Andrew has entered into a secret agreement with a commercial giant that will see him act as a network intermediary, a movement that will beat him millions.
The dishonored Royal will work with the Dutch firm Startupbootcamp (SBC), sharing valuable contacts made during the Dragons Pitch@Palace style initiative, a project that connected entrepreneurs with investors.
SBC senior staff initially launched the idea to Buckingham Palace last summer, before finally sealing the agreement with the Duke of York.
A source said The sun That the Duke win money from each agreement that SBC ensures and that the unexpected gain will help to cling to Royal Lodge, a real grade II property in Windsor Great Park and the current residence of the Prince.
“It is a way of exploiting the enviable commercial links he has assured over the years,” they said.
Weeks after the SBC agreement was floating, the king obtained his annual funds of £ 1 million for his brother, whom he had been trying to evict Royal Lodge.
Prince Andrew has entered a secret agreement with the Dutch firm Startupbootcamp that will act as a network intermediary, a movement that will beat him millions
Weeks after the SBC agreement was floating, the king withdrew his annual funds of £ 1 million for his brother, whom he had been trying to evict Royal Lodge (in the photo)
The future of the Pitch@Palace scheme was in doubt after the disastrous Newsnight interview of the Duke about the links to the dead pedophile Jeffrey Epstein (the couple that is shown together in New York in 2010)
But Andrew has not yet abandoned the Windsor house, with sources of palace insured on its financing flows.
It was discovered in January that more than 230,000 pitch@palace had been extracted, according to recent accounts documents.
During the financial year until March 31, 2024, the amount of cash by hand and in the bank in the company decreased by half, from £ 454,979 to £ 220,990.
The accounts, which were presented to the company’s house on December 30, showed that the retirement was signed by the only director of Pitch@Palace, Arthur Lancaster, on behalf of the Board.
Last year, around £ 120,000 of the Pitch@Palace Global Ltd account were also extracted with their total assets that fell from £ 610,870 to £ 489,915.
It occurred in the midst of concerns about the future of the scheme after the disastrous Newsnight interview of the Duke about the links to the dead pedophile Jeffrey Epstein.
The scheme was also at risk after it arose that a former head of the company was an alleged spy.
As for his new company, the CEO of Startupbootcamp Kauan von Novack said: ‘Our mission is to help entrepreneurs create the change that the world needs.
“We see an immense value in the network built by pitch@palace.”
Mailonline has contacted the Duke of York and the startupbootcamp to comment.
